'''LaGrange''' ({{IPAc-en|l|ə|ˈ|g|r|eɪ|n|dʒ}} {{respell|lə|GRAYNJ}}) is a [[Administrative divisions of New York#Town|town]] in [[Dutchess County, New York|Dutchess County]], [[New York (state)|New York]], United States. The population was 15,975 at the 2020 census.<ref name="Census 2010">{{cite web| url=http://factfinder.census.gov/bkmk/table/1.0/en/DEC/10_SF1/G001/0600000US3602740299| title=Geographic Identifiers: 2010 Demographic Profile Data (G001): La Grange town, Dutchess County, New York| publisher=U.S. Census Bureau, American Factfinder| access-date=November 12, 2015| archive-url=https://archive.today/20200213130932/http://factfinder.census.gov/bkmk/table/1.0/en/DEC/10_SF1/G001/0600000US3602740299| archive-date=February 13, 2020| url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>United States Census Bureau, 2020 Report, LaGrange town, New York</ref>  The town was named after the estate of the [[Marquis de Lafayette]].<ref>{{cite book | url=https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_9V1IAAAAMAAJ | title=The Origin of Certain Place Names in the United States | publisher=[[United States Government Publishing Office|Government Printing Office]] | author=Gannett, Henry | year=1905 | pages=[https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_9V1IAAAAMAAJ/page/n178 179]}}</ref>

==History==
[[File:LaGrange District School, Freedom Plains, NY.jpg|thumb|left|Old LaGrange District School, in Freedom Plains]]
The [[Administrative divisions of New York#Town|town]] was originally established in 1821 as "Freedom" from parts of the towns of [[Beekman, New York|Beekman]] and [[Fishkill (town), New York|Fishkill]]. Confusion with [[Freedom, New York|Freedom]], a town in [[Cattaraugus County, New York|Cattaraugus County]] that had been settled ten years earlier and established one year earlier, caused the name to be changed to "LaGrange" in 1828.

==Geography==
According to the [[United States Census Bureau]], the town has a total area of {{convert|104.5|km2|order=flip}}, of which {{convert|103.3|km2|order=flip}} is land and {{convert|1.2|km2|order=flip}}, or 1.17%, is water.<ref name="Census 2010"/> The town of LaGrange is located within the [[Hudson Valley]] region of New York. The towns bordering LaGrange are [[Union Vale, New York|Union Vale]] to the east, [[Beekman, New York|Beekman]] to the southeast, [[East Fishkill, New York|East Fishkill]] and [[Wappinger, New York|Wappinger]] to the south, [[Poughkeepsie (town), New York|Poughkeepsie]] to the west, and [[Pleasant Valley (town), New York|Pleasant Valley]] to the north, with a small part of [[Washington, New York|Washington]] also bordering LaGrange.

===Roads===
Three state highways bisect the town and connect it with other towns in Dutchess County and the surrounding area. The [[Taconic State Parkway]] is a north–south parkway through LaGrange. [[James Baird State Park]], which provides a golf course, playground, sports fields, and hiking and cycling trails, is located in LaGrange along the Taconic Parkway. The parkway also serves as an important commuter road for LaGrange, connecting the town to points south, including [[White Plains, New York|White Plains]] {{convert|51|mi}} and [[New York City]], {{convert|75|mi}} to the south.

[[New York State Route 55]] is an east–west road that goes through the center of the town; [[Arlington High School (New York)|Arlington High School]], the Freedom Plains United Presbyterian Church, and multiple shops and stores are located on a two-mile section of Route 55 in [[Freedom Plains, New York|Freedom Plains]], a hamlet of LaGrange. In the summer and fall of 2014, three [[traffic circle]]s were added to this stretch of Route 55 in Freedom Plains in an effort to ease congestion and also to beautify this part of LaGrange. To the west, Route 55 connects LaGrange to the city of [[Poughkeepsie, New York|Poughkeepsie]], the closest urbanized area to LaGrange; to the east, Route 55 connects LaGrange to the town of [[Pawling (town), New York|Pawling]] and the [[New York State Route 22|Route 22]] corridor. It is located halfway between Poughkeepsie and Pawling, about {{convert|11|mi}} from both.

[[New York State Route 82]] is a highway that goes southwest–northeast through the town, from [[Hopewell Junction, New York|Hopewell Junction]] to Moores Mills. Route 82 connects LaGrange with [[Millbrook, New York|Millbrook]] to the north and Hopewell Junction to the south.

There are also several county roads that go in various parts of the town.

==Parks and recreation==
{{Unreferenced section|date=August 2022}}
Freedom Park is the largest and most extensive park belonging to the town of LaGrange. At the park, there is a small, spring-fed lake in which patrons are permitted to swim under the supervision of [[Red Cross]]-trained lifeguards. There is a set of eight 25-yard lap lanes that enables the town to support a swim team. There is a concession that sells snacks at the lake. Freedom Park also boasts a bandstand and a large, permanent, open-air pavilion; there is a small playground as well. Each summer, a day camp is offered by the town at Freedom Park.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Freedom Park |url=https://www.lagrangeny.gov/departments/parks-recreation/discover-parks/freedom-park |access-date=October 8, 2023 |website=Town of LaGrange |language=en-US}}</ref>

Other parks in LaGrange include Stringham Park, an extensive complex of soccer fields located on Stringham Road in the west of the town, and [[James Baird State Park]], which provides a golf course, playground, and cycling and hiking trails.<ref>{{Cite web |title=LaGrangeville Parks & Gardens {{!}} Stringham Park {{!}} Dutchess CountyParks & Gardens {{!}} Hudson Valley Parks & Gardens |url=https://dutchesstourism.com/listingsv/stringham-park |access-date=October 8, 2023 |website=dutchesstourism.com |language=en-us}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title= James Baird State Park|url=https://parks.ny.gov/documents/parks/JamesBairdTrailMap.pdf |publisher=New York State Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation}}</ref>

As of the [[census]]<ref name="GR2">{{cite web|url=https://www.census.gov|publisher=[[United States Census Bureau]]|access-date=January 31, 2008|title=U.S. Census website}}</ref> of 2000, there were 14,928 people, 5,085 households, and 4,103 families residing in the town.  The population density was {{convert|376.0|PD/sqmi|PD/km2|sp=us|adj=off}}.  There were 5,240 housing units at an average density of {{convert|132.0|/sqmi|/km2|sp=us|adj=off}}.  The racial makeup of the town was 91.98% [[White (U.S. Census)|White]], 2.41% [[African American (U.S. Census)|African American]], 0.12% [[Native American (U.S. Census)|Native American]], 2.94% [[Asian (U.S. Census)|Asian]], 1.14% from [[Race (United States Census)|other races]], and 1.41% from two or more races. [[Hispanic (U.S. Census)|Hispanic]] or [[Latino (U.S. Census)|Latino]] of any race were 4.26% of the population.

There were 5,085 households, out of which 40.6% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 71.2% were [[Marriage|married couples]] living together, 6.5% had a female householder with no husband present, and 19.3% were non-families. 15.4% of all households were made up of individuals, and 5.5% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.  The average household size was 2.93 and the average family size was 3.28.

In the town, the population was spread out, with 28.5% under the age of 18, 5.9% from 18 to 24, 29.9% from 25 to 44, 25.3% from 45 to 64, and 10.4% who were 65 years of age or older.  The median age was 38 years. For every 100 females, there were 97.5 males.  For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 96.0 males.

The median income for a household in the town was $74,881, and the median income for a family was $80,724. Males had a median income of $61,806 versus $36,955 for females. The [[per capita income]] for the town was $27,872.  About 1.7% of families and 3.7% of the population were below the [[poverty line]], including 4.2% of those under age 18 and 2.4% of those age 65 or over.

==Communities and locations in LaGrange==
*'''Arthursburg''' – A hamlet at the southern town line. It is named after [[Chester A. Arthur]], twenty-first president of the United States.
*'''Billings''' – A [[Hamlet (place)|hamlet]] north of LaGrangeville.
*[[Freedom Plains, New York|Freedom Plains]] – A hamlet northwest of LaGrangeville.
*[[James Baird State Park]] – A [[state park]] in the northern part of the town.
*'''LaGrangeville''' (or '''La Grangeville''')– A hamlet in the southeastern part of the town.<ref>{{cite gnis |id=954889| name=LaGrangeville}}</ref>
**LaGrangeville is an area in LaGrange with the zip code of 12540. As of 2014, this area had a population of 8,221, which makes it the largest part of LaGrange. 
*'''Manchester Bridge''' – A hamlet in the western part of the town.
*'''Moores Mill''' – A location in the northeastern part of the town.
*'''Noxon''' – A location west of LaGrangeville.
*[[Red Oaks Mill, New York|Red Oaks Mill]] – A suburb of [[Poughkeepsie, New York|Poughkeepsie city]] that is also located in [[Poughkeepsie (town), New York|Poughkeepsie town]].
*'''Rombout Ridge''' – A location near the western town line.
*'''Titus''' – A hamlet near the western town line.
*[[Titusville, New York|Titusville]] – A hamlet in the southwestern part of the town, north of Red Oaks Mill.

==Schools==
[[Arlington High School (LaGrange, New York)|Arlington High School]] and [[LaGrange Middle School]] of the [[Arlington Central School District]] are in LaGrange, as are several of the School District's primary, elementary and intermediate schools.
